scope: Theorem A.1 (Tensor packing) of the manuscript “Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations” (preprints/Pointwise-Multiple-Ergodic-Averages-for-Mixing-Transformations-October-4-2026/multiple-ergodic-averages.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 154 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b9d8fcffac455475), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a universal constant C with the following property. Let 0 < ε ≤ 1, and let d ≥ 1 and L ≥ 0 be integers. Let x1, . . . , xm and y1, . . . , ym lie in the unit balls of real Hilbert spaces H1, H2. For each family suppose that a graph on {1, . . . , m} of maximum degree at most L contains every off-diagonal pair whose absolute inner product exceeds η, where 0 ≤ η ≤ ε2 /104 . The two exceptional graphs may differ. For every orthogonal projection P on H1 ⊗ H2 of rank at most d, #{j : ∥P(xj ⊗ yj)∥ ≥ ε} ≤ C(1 + L)ε−2 exp (︂ Cε−2 √ d log(2 + d) )︂ . (A.1) For d = dm as defined in (4.4), this is oε,L(m), uniformly over the Hilbert spaces, vectors, projections, and allowed values of η.
